passage: Sunday night. I wrote something in the calendar today and it felt like signing a contract with myself: "Dinner with Zainab, 8 pm, weeknights, unmovable" and "Sunday call with Ammi and Abbu, 11 am". I made them events, not reminders, and put my wife's name on the invite. My reasoning: when a boundary is only mine, I can talk myself out of it for one "quick" late meeting. But when somebody is waiting at the table, I can't. Zainab laughed when the invite arrived, then said it was the nicest one she had ever had. On Friday I will see if it holds when the launch gets busy. If it does, I will know it works because it is tied to people, not to willpower. - Zubin

passage:
In the kasba, the cooperative bank pulled its shutters down at five, but Pradeep kept carrying ledgers home in a cloth bag. Most nights his wife Nazia ate before him, and the Sunday phone call to his parents in the village kept slipping to "next week".
One evening, sitting on the front steps while the neighbour milked her buffalo, he worked it out aloud to Nazia. "When I tell myself I'll stop at eight, there's no one to stop for. The ledgers win. But if you're sitting at the table, I can't pretend."
He took the calendar off the kitchen wall and wrote in thick pen: every night, 8 pm, dinner. Sunday, 10 am, call Amma and Appa.
"Unmovable?" Nazia asked.
"Unmovable. If the bank manager asks, I'll say I have an appointment."
She laughed. "You do."

qa.q: What did Pradeep write on the calendar?
qa.a: Every night, 8 pm, dinner, and Sunday, 10 am, call Amma and Appa.

qa.q: What is Pradeep feeling when he says there's no one to stop for?
qa.a: He is frustrated that his own promise to stop at eight never holds, and hopeful that someone waiting will give the limit real weight.

qa.q: What else could help if the ledgers still pile up before eight?
qa.a: Pradeep could leave the ledgers at the bank and tell the manager which tasks will be done next morning, so the calendar block isn't fighting unfinished work.

qa.q: How might Nazia feel about the new calendar entries?
qa.a: Nazia is likely pleased and amused, since she no longer eats before him and her joke shows dinner now counts as a real appointment.

grounding: It shows a man deciding that dinner with his wife and a Sunday call to his parents are fixed calendar events, because having someone waiting makes the limit hold.
